problem: Existing VLN surveys organize prior work by technical taxonomies and do not systematically characterize the paradigm shift from passive instruction following on closed benchmarks to autonomous cognitive navigation in open-world settings.
motivation: VLN has expanded from closed, single indoor benchmarks such as R2R to open-world environments. Understanding the evolutionary logic connecting the technical lines is needed to guide research toward trustworthy open-world deployment.
key_idea: An evolution-centered unified analytical framework that reviews VLN across four progressive layers: perception, cognition, learning, and generalization.
insight: Based on the abstract only: the survey claims that viewing VLN as a capability evolution, rather than a technical taxonomy, reveals the intrinsic connections among technical lines. It identifies open challenges at each of the four layers. No ablations or empirical analysis are available from the abstract.
method: Perception layer: reviews how VLN agents ground language in visual perception, as part of the four-layer framework.
Cognition layer: reviews reasoning and decision-making for navigation.
Learning layer: reviews how navigation capabilities are learned and trained.
Generalization layer: reviews transfer from closed benchmarks to open-world environments.

Evolution-centered synthesis: links the layers to trace the shift from passive instruction following to autonomous cognitive navigation, and identifies open challenges and future directions per layer.
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no experimental results reported
results: This is a survey and the abstract reports no quantitative results. It contributes an evolution-centered four-layer framework (perception, cognition, learning, generalization), open challenges per layer, and a roadmap toward trustworthy open-world deployment.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details of coverage and taxonomy are unknown.
As a survey, it offers no new empirical validation.
builds_on: Room-to-Room (R2R) benchmark line of VLN research
compares_to: Existing VLN surveys organized by technical taxonomy
